**The plan: Paris → Lyon → Annecy, Sat 17 – Sun 25 Oct 2026** (9 days/8 nights, 42 days out — comfortably beyond the 30-day window)

Key decisions, based on details I verified online:
- **Dates:** placed inside the French Toussaint school holidays (17 Oct – 2 Nov 2026) so the child misses no school; the document flags the trade-off (book early, trains fill) and notes clocks go back on the final morning.
- **Rail spine, all direct and family-friendly:** Paris Gare de Lyon → Lyon Part-Dieu ≈2h00; Lyon → Annecy ≈1h55–2h30; Annecy → Paris ≈3h45. Only two moves in nine days, with mid-morning departures rather than early alarms.
- **Closure-proofed sequencing:** the Louvre is scheduled on the Monday (when Orsay, Versailles and the Cité des Sciences are all shut) and Orsay on the Tuesday (when the Louvre shuts); the Musée des Confluences is on a Thursday (closed Mondays) and the Château d'Annecy on a Saturday (closed Tuesdays, Oct–May).
- **Balance:** four short museums never on consecutive days, an outdoor block every day (Luxembourg sailboats, Seine cruise, Fourvière, Parc de la Tête d'Or, the flat car-free Voie Verte lake ride), food anchors (bouchon lunches, Les Halles Paul Bocuse, Savoyard dinner), and a deliberate apartment/park break daily.

Two caveats worth noting: the Lake Annecy one-hour cruise runs March–November but October sailings depend on weather and demand, so it's marked "check the board at the quay," with a rainy-day alternative; and all opening days should be re-confirmed about a week before travel, since the document reflects what was published at planning time. Indicative budget for the family, excluding international flights: roughly €3,150–3,900.
